note: Hand-written per-matchup write-ups for the Scores tab, keyed "week|matchup_id", rendered in the click-to-open strip at the foot of each match card. 2026 is written LIVE, week by week -- see Phase 8. Facts sourced from scripts/build_matchup_facts.py; check every number before it goes in. Consolation games with nothing at stake deliberately get no entry.

shape.headline: one line, the game in a sentence
shape.body: 3-4 sentences, Hall of Fame & Shame roast level. Real point figures stay in the prose -- points are a scale everyone reads natively.
shape.tags: optional array of short uppercase labels, e.g. UPSET / BLOWOUT / UNLUCKY LOSS

1|1.headline: SirWinsAlot starts two duds and still posts the best Week 1 score in league history
1|1.body: Jared Hayes scored 214.46 with Colston Loveland at 0.00 and Jaylen Waddle at 0.70 in the lineup and Tyler Shough's 25.20 watching from the bench. Caleb Williams went for 37.26, Ashton Jeanty added 31.20, and a manager who was 0-4 against Jake Blackwell before Sunday won by 68.56. The defending champion got 12.15 from Puka Nacua and 4.10 from Chig Okonkwo, with Pat Freiermuth's 17.10 sitting on the bench.

1|2.headline: Same opponent, same Week 1, nearly the same score, opposite result
1|2.body: A year ago Erin Jacobs opened the season by beating Chris Merkel with 157.29. This year Erin scored 158.23 in the rematch, within a point of it, and lost by 17.86, because Chris started Isaiah Likely at the second tight end spot and got 30.55 back. Derrick Henry went for 35.30 in Erin's opener for the second straight year, and Omarion Hampton answered with 8.30. Mark Andrews managed 10.65, six times last September's output, and nobody is calling it a comeback.

1|3.headline: Matt Bova gets 0.52 from the quarterback spot and a zero from Romeo Doubs
1|3.body: Matt Bova started Sam Darnold, who returned 0.52, and Romeo Doubs, who returned nothing at all, and finished on 85.77, the lowest score of the week. Mike Gesicki's 20.80 sat on the bench, but even the best possible lineup would have come up 33 short. Chris Bova was under projection too, with Bo Nix posting 5.44 and Chuba Hubbard's 22.95 benched, and won by 71.48 anyway behind Jahmyr Gibbs (32.10) and Trey McBride (27.50).

1|4.headline: Nabers in Paris ends an 0-5 run against Duane with a below-median 131.79
1|4.body: Duane Gillenwater had won all five regular-season meetings before Sunday. Nick Bova broke the streak with Christian McCaffrey at 11.55, James Cook — fresh off 8.20 in last year's final — at 8.65, and Dallas Goedert's 26.45 benched behind AJ Barner's 3.55; Jalen Coker's 33.80 covered for all of it. Trade Block Maye! got 9.82 from Drake Maye, a rough day for the namesake, and started Jake Ferguson (2.85) over T.J. Hockenson (14.85) in a game lost by 13.44.

1|5.headline: BoKnows723 wins by 108.46, the second-biggest beating in league history
1|5.body: Jake Bogardus got 32.40 from D'Andre Swift in a flex spot, 29.20 from Justin Jefferson, 27.90 from David Montgomery, and 48.62 from Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes at quarterback. Starting Terry McLaurin (2.90) over Kyle Monangai (21.15) was the only blemish. Mitch Blackwell scored 86.06 on Jordan Addison 0.00, Quentin Johnston 3.20, and Jayden Reed 4.25, and the whole bench combined for 33.52, so the answer was not sitting there either.

1|6.headline: Josh Allen scores 37.66 and gets no help whatsoever
1|6.body: Andrew Bova came in as the league's all-time head-to-head leader and got 37.66 from Josh Allen and 16.85 from the entire running back room, with Tony Pollard at 3.40 and George Kittle at 3.70. Nick Merkel got 7.30 combined from Ja'Marr Chase and A.J. Brown and it did not matter: Bryce Young scored 33.44 out of the superflex, more than double the projection, and Bijan Robinson added 29.80. Final: 163.99 to 126.61.

2|1.headline: SirWinsAlot benches the right quarterback again and wins on the wrong ones
2|1.body: Jared Hayes got 7.72 from Caleb Williams and 6.16 from Trevor Lawrence, left Tyler Shough's 22.38 on the bench for the second week in a row, and watched Colston Loveland follow last week's 0.00 with 1.30. It still won by 27.24, because Jonathan Taylor went for 28.45 and three receivers cleared 20. Erin Jacobs got 28.35 from Travis Kelce and 1.10 from Jonathon Brooks in a flex spot, with Tre Tucker's 24.65 sitting on the bench, and 114.49 was never going to cover that.

2|2.headline: Josh Allen finally gets help, and it comes from the tight end room
2|2.body: Andrew Bova started the week 0-2 and scored 174.43, 65.85 above an honest projection: Josh Allen went for 42.82, Dak Prescott added 29.76, and Dalton Schultz (29.75) and George Kittle (20.50) combined for 50.25 at tight end. Nico Collins still sat in the lineup for 0.00. Jake Bogardus scored 134.53, above the median, but David Montgomery managed 3.90 and Justin Jefferson 8.25, and the first loss of BoKnows723's season arrived by 39.90.

2|3.headline: Chris Merkel starts Jaxson Dart for 0.80 and Davante Adams makes it not matter
2|3.body: Chris Merkel had Matthew Stafford's 26.98 on the bench and Jaxson Dart's 0.80 in the lineup, and 128.02 was below the median. Davante Adams saved the day with 40.00. Matt Bova's bench combined for 17.69, so there was no rescue there either, and Devin Singletary (0.90), J.K. Dobbins (3.60) and Tucker Kraft (4.25) left Drew Lock's 23.40 as the best thing in the lineup. At 95.87, Love's Shack posted the week's lowest score for the second straight week.

2|4.headline: Nick Merkel wins with 111.01, a negative from DJ Moore, and 3.00 from Saquon
2|4.body: McConkey Kong scored 20.55 below an honest projection and stayed perfect in head-to-head anyway. Saquon Barkley made 3.00, Bijan Robinson 9.60, DJ Moore finished at -0.10, and Denzel Boston's 20.75 watched from the bench. Duane Gillenwater could not take advantage: Drake Maye (8.02) and Carson Wentz (6.32) combined for 14.34 at quarterback, and he is 0-4.

2|5.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba scores 42.00 and Mitch Blackwell still loses by 80
2|5.body: Mitch Blackwell got 42.00 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and 20.02 from Cam Ward, and 3.85 from the whole running back room, with Mike Washington at 0.70. Jayden Reed (0.90), Alec Pierce (2.10) and Quentin Johnston (2.15) rounded out a 99.73. Chris Bova scored 180.11 on CeeDee Lamb's 34.55 and 51.40 from his backs, left just 11.75 on the table, and is 4-0.

2|6.headline: The defending champion beats Nick Bova for the first time in five tries
2|6.body: Jake Blackwell was 0-4 against Nabers in Paris before Sunday and scored the week's best 181.29 to end it: Jared Goff (29.78) and Brock Purdy (28.48) at quarterback, 34.20 from Amon-Ra St. Brown, 26.20 from DeVonta Smith. Nick Bova benched Dallas Goedert for 26.45 last week, started him this week for 1.40, and left Darren Waller's 19.55 on the bench. Malik Nabers, the team's namesake, scored 0.60, and 138.43 lost by 42.86.

3|1.headline: Matt Bova wins one, and it takes two quarterbacks and a Mitch Blackwell to do it
3|1.body: Love's Shack got 45.14 from Sam Darnold (26.66) and Jordan Love (18.48) plus 20.75 from Tee Higgins, and the first win of the season arrived at 130.94, still below the median. Hunter Henry scored 1.75 in the flex with Mike Gesicki's 13.70 on the bench. Mitch Blackwell beat an honest projection by 37.69 and got 34.36 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, then lost by 12.46 with one quarterback in the lineup, Cam Ward at 9.44, and Emari Demercado starting for 0.00. Mitch is 0-6, and Matt now leads the all-time series 3-1.

3|2.headline: Jake Blackwell's two Brocks score 64.63, and Duane Gillenwater's quarterbacks score 9.88
3|2.body: Nacua Matata scored 182.44, a second straight week over 180, with Brock Purdy at 33.28, Brock Bowers at 31.35 and Michael Wilson at 23.65, and Jacoby Brissett's 25.60 still sat on the bench. Duane Gillenwater got 3.76 from Drake Maye and 6.12 from Jameis Winston, started T.J. Hockenson for 3.60 with Kenyon Sadiq's 26.75 on the bench, and left 51.28 on the table, the most of the week. Duane is 0-6, and the all-time series is level at 2-2.

3|3.headline: Nick Merkel benches Geno Smith's 26.04 and loses by 1.74
3|3.body: McConkey Kong started Malik Willis for 10.00 with Geno Smith's 26.04 on the bench, a 16.04-point swap that would have covered a 1.74-point loss nine times over. Bijan Robinson went for 35.80 and Ja'Marr Chase 23.30, while Brian Thomas made 1.55 and Terrance Ferguson 2.15. Jake Bogardus scored 133.78, 0.10 below the median, on 29.40 from Drake London and 5.20 from Justin Jefferson, and took the head-to-head win anyway to go 3-2 all-time against Nick.

3|4.headline: SirWinsAlot finally starts Tyler Shough, and nobody can catch it
3|4.body: After two weeks of benching him, Jared Hayes started Tyler Shough and got 23.80, plus 19.78 from Trevor Lawrence and 24.55 from Juwan Johnson, for 157.53. Jonathan Taylor followed last week's 28.45 with 8.20 and it did not matter. Chris Merkel scored 133.99, 0.11 above the median, and lost by 23.54 with Marcus Mariota's 20.42 on the bench behind Baker Mayfield's 13.28 and 13.55 from his two running backs combined. Hayes is 6-0; Chris Merkel still leads the all-time series 3-2.

3|5.headline: Nick Bova posts the week's low and hands the family series to Andrew
3|5.body: Nabers in Paris scored 103.41, 40.31 below an honest projection: De'Von Achane made 1.70, Adonai Mitchell 0.00, Daniel Jones 7.90, and Malik Nabers, the namesake, 5.85 after last week's 0.60. Kirk Cousins (22.22) and Christian McCaffrey (21.35) were the only reasons it cleared 100. Andrew Bova won by 40.64 on George Kittle's 29.20 and Jaylen Warren's 20.35, despite starting Blake Corum for 2.00 with Konata Mumpfield's 20.05 and Aaron Rodgers' 22.68 on the bench, and now leads the all-time series 3-2.

3|6.headline: Chris Bova scores 235.30, and Erin Jacobs' fourth-best score of the week loses by 91
3|6.body: Titsburg Feelers posted the second-highest regular-season total in league history, behind a 246.52 from 2023: Jahmyr Gibbs went for 40.40, Kyren Williams, Bhayshul Tuten and Chuba Hubbard added 50.05 more, and Harold Fannin (25.85) and Trey McBride (18.75) made 44.60 at tight end. That was 73.87 above an honest projection. Erin Jacobs beat the median with 144.26, got 21.75 from Matthew Golden and 21.40 from Derrick Henry, and lost by 91.04. Chris Bova is 6-0 and 3-1 all-time against her.

4|1.headline: Jared Hayes beats Jake Bogardus for the first time, and gets to 7-0 doing it
4|1.body: Four meetings, four losses, and then 171.37 to 151.88: Javonte Williams went for 29.30, and a Hayes lineup that finished 3.48 under an honest projection was plenty. Jake got 43.70 from Tetairoa McMillan, the best start in the league this week, and gave it back by starting Rashee Rice for 0.00 with Kyle Monangai's 27.50 on the bench, more than the 19.49 margin on its own. Bogardus still leads the all-time series 4-1, but after sweeping Hayes in 2025 he trails the 2026 rivalry series 1-0 by 19.49 going into game 2 in Week 13.

4|2.headline: Mitch Blackwell has his best day of the season and loses by 70
4|2.body: Mitch scored 124.28, his season high and 24.72 above an honest projection, behind Sam LaPorta's 24.40 and 20.75 from Dohnte Meyers, a receiver Sleeper projected for 3.79. Jake Blackwell answered with 194.55, the high score of the week and his third straight over 180, on Kenneth Walker's 31.40, Puka Nacua's 26.45 and Brock Bowers' 22.85, with Joe Burrow's 25.72 sitting on the bench. That makes Jake 5-1 all-time against Mitch and puts him 1-0 up in the 2026 rivalry series by 70.27 heading into Week 13. Mitch is 0-7.

4|3.headline: Matt Bova takes the rivalry opener for the second year running, and Duane's bench watches
4|3.body: Matt put up 166.46, 41.79 above an honest projection and the best mark against expectation in the league, with Tee Higgins at 25.95, Romeo Doubs at 22.80 and Carnell Tate at 20.75. Duane posted his own season high, 147.46, and lost it at flex: Kenyon Sadiq started for 0.00 while T.J. Hockenson scored 28.40 on the bench, which alone would have covered the 19.00 margin, and his 65.08 left on the table was the most in the league. The all-time series is now 3-3, Matt leads the 2026 rivalry series 1-0 by 19.00 with game 2 in Week 13, and Duane is 0-7.

4|4.headline: Titsburg Feelers run it up on Nabers in Paris
4|4.body: CeeDee Lamb went for 38.05 and Kyren Williams for 33.95, and Chris Bova's running backs alone put up 86.65 in a 182.48 that keeps him unbeaten at 7-0. Nick started Daniel Jones for 7.92 with Kirk Cousins' 22.60 on the bench, got 1.95 from Dalton Kincaid and 0.90 from Courtland Sutton, and finished 37.25 under an honest projection, the worst mark in the league this week. His namesake Malik Nabers did show up with 22.45, which is how it stayed a 58.28 loss. Chris goes 4-1 all-time against Nick and leads the 2026 rivalry series 1-0 by 58.28 heading into Week 13, a year after Nick took the 2025 series on points.

4|5.headline: Erin Jacobs posts the week's low, and her best lineup would have lost too
4|5.body: Erin scored 108.08, her lowest of the season and 28.32 under an honest projection, with Travis Kelce at 4.25, Jeremiyah Love at 5.50 and her two quarterbacks combining for 23.08. Her best possible lineup was 120.13, which still loses to Andrew Bova by 38.84. Andrew's 158.97 ran through Nico Collins' 31.05 and George Kittle's 18.75, and he still benched Aaron Rodgers' 21.96 to start two quarterbacks who scored less. Andrew leads the 2026 rivalry series 1-0 by 50.89 going into Week 13, and the all-time record against Erin he inherited from CCJ with the Joshin Around roster goes to 3-2.

4|6.headline: Merkel derby: Chris wins the family game with 57.65 left on his bench
4|6.body: Neither Merkel cracked 140: Chris won 136.65 to 116.62 while starting Parker Washington for 1.87 and Marcus Mariota for 5.34, with Keon Coleman's 23.10 on the bench. Nick got 28.20 from Bijan Robinson and 21.46 from Bryce Young, then 1.50 from Saquon Barkley, 4.95 from Ja'Marr Chase, 2.70 from DJ Moore and 0.00 from Ladd McConkey. Zay Flowers' 25.05 and Alvin Kamara's 21.30 carried Chris to the lowest winning score of the week and a 20.03 margin. He goes up 3-2 all-time and leads the 2026 rivalry series 1-0 into Week 13, after Nick took the 2025 series on points.

5|1.headline: Tyler Shough scores -0.16, and Jared Hayes' perfect start goes with him
5|1.body: The league's two unbeaten teams met, and SirWinsAlot brought 95.13, 59.71 below an honest projection and the worst miss of the season. Tyler Shough went for -0.16, Chris Olave, Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele added 19.55 between them, and Trevor Lawrence's 23.74 was the only start that beat its projection. Titsburg Feelers won by 67.39 on Jahmyr Gibbs' 36.70 and Garrett Wilson's 22.90, despite CeeDee Lamb at 2.15, Harold Fannin at 1.40 and Bo Nix starting for 7.92 over Jayden Daniels' 32.26, and still finished 0.60 below the median. Chris Bova is 8-1 and leads the all-time series 4-1.

5|2.headline: Nick Bova's best week of the year beats the median and runs into Tyler Huntley
5|2.body: Nabers in Paris scored 163.71, a season high and 0.59 above the median, with George Pickens at 27.00, Malik Nabers at 26.60 and James Cook at 22.55. It met the week's high: Jake Bogardus got 32.00 from Bucky Irving, 23.65 from Tyler Warren and 24.04 from Tyler Huntley at superflex, and scored 184.54, 34.19 above an honest projection and the best mark of the week. Nick started KC Concepcion for 1.25 with Kevin Coleman's 12.12 on the bench, Dalton Kincaid made 3.95, and his best possible lineup, 185.48, would have won by 0.94. The all-time series is level at 2-2.

5|3.headline: Jake Blackwell's quarterbacks score 55.54, and Brian Thomas starts for zero
5|3.body: Nacua Matata cleared 170 for a fourth straight week, 173.76, with Puka Nacua at 33.45, Jared Goff and Joe Burrow at 55.54 combined, and Brock Bowers and Pat Freiermuth adding 48.50 at tight end. The running backs made 10.90 and it did not matter. Nick Merkel started Brian Thomas for 0.00, got 14.80 from Bijan Robinson against a 24.82 projection, and lost by 51.53. Jake Blackwell is 7-2 and leads the all-time series 4-1.

5|4.headline: Matt Bova follows the league's best week against projection with one of its worst
5|4.body: A week after beating an honest projection by 41.79, Love's Shack finished 40.50 below one at 88.88. Tee Higgins, Romeo Doubs, Cooper Kupp and Carnell Tate combined for 10.90, RJ Harvey made 0.70, and Jordan Love's 29.28 was a third of the team's total. Andrew Bova posted his season high, 177.89, on Jaylen Warren's 36.30, Josh Allen's 30.50 and Mike Evans' 25.55, with Aaron Rodgers' 24.00 on the bench behind Dak Prescott's 12.64, and won by 89.01, the widest margin of the week. Andrew leads the all-time series 3-1.

5|5.headline: Duane Gillenwater's quarterbacks score 65.20, and Trade Block Maye! finally wins one
5|5.body: Two weeks after his quarterbacks combined for 9.88, Drake Maye went for 39.46 and Jameis Winston 25.74, Christian Watson added 33.55, and Duane posted his season high, 174.92, for his first win of 2026. Erin Jacobs scored her season low, 98.05: Michael Mayer made 1.20 at tight end, Jeremiyah Love 2.20, and DeMario Douglas' 22.00 sat on the bench as she left 61.11 on the table, the most of the week. Duane won by 76.87 and leads the all-time series 5-0.

5|6.headline: Mitch Blackwell posts the lowest score of the season with one quarterback and a zero
5|6.body: Medical Tent Mafia scored 84.18, the lowest total of 2026, with Cam Ward the only quarterback in the lineup at 5.00, Darnell Washington at superflex for 3.70, Jordan Addison starting for 0.00 and 7.35 from three running backs. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Sam LaPorta made 22.05 each, and the best possible lineup was still only 96.38. Chris Merkel won by 83.43 on Isaiah Likely's 35.65, Parker Washington's 31.34 and Matthew Stafford's 27.32, despite starting Alvin Kamara for 0.60 with MarShawn Lloyd's 16.45 on the bench. Mitch is 0-9 and still leads the all-time series 4-2.

6|1.headline: Nick Bova ends a four-game skid with the week's high, and Chris Merkel's bench could have stopped him
6|1.body: Nabers in Paris scored 178.10, a season high and 42.31 above an honest projection, the best mark of the week, with Christian McCaffrey at 27.45, Malik Nabers at 27.25, James Cook at 24.05 and two quarterbacks at 43.50 combined; Darren Waller started for 0.00 with Dallas Goedert's 14.10 on the bench. Chris Merkel posted his season low, 122.81, starting Mark Andrews at flex for 1.40 with Jaylin Noel's 24.38 on the bench and getting 4.60 from MarShawn Lloyd and Rhamondre Stevenson. He left 60.63 on the table, the most of the week, and his best possible lineup, 183.44, would have won by 5.34. Nick won by 55.29 and leads the all-time series 3-2.

6|2.headline: Jacoby Brissett scores 6.92, and Jake Blackwell beats Andrew Bova for the first time anyway
6|2.body: Nacua Matata's run of four straight 170-point weeks ended at 143.08, a season low, with Brissett at 6.92, Cam Skattebo starting for 0.00 while Tyrone Tracy's 20.30 sat on the bench, and Puka Nacua at 13.50 against a 22.98 projection; Kenneth Walker's 27.40 and DeVonta Smith's 19.50 carried it. Andrew Bova finished 7.96 below an honest projection at 129.92: Josh Allen made 18.30, Nico Collins 11.90, and Dak Prescott started at superflex for 11.02 with Aaron Rodgers' 16.02 on the bench. Jake won by 13.16 for his first win over Andrew in five meetings, and Andrew leads the all-time series 4-1.

6|3.headline: Chris Bova's worst week of the year still wins by 39, because Bijan Robinson made 5.30
6|3.body: Titsburg Feelers posted a season low, 137.38, with Bo Nix starting at quarterback for 4.48, Kyren Williams at 8.70 against a 21.28 projection, Harold Fannin at 2.15 and Kyle Pitts' 25.00 on the bench; Bhayshul Tuten's 23.95 and Jayden Daniels' 21.00 covered for it. Nick Merkel was worse: 98.12, his own season low and 24.19 below an honest projection, the worst miss of the week. Bijan Robinson made 5.30 against a 25.57 projection, and A.J. Brown, Brandin Cooks, Denzel Boston and Ladd McConkey combined for 12.45. Chris Bova won by 39.26, is 10-1 and the league's last unbeaten head to head, and leads the all-time series 3-2.

6|4.headline: Mitch Blackwell breaks his own record for the season's lowest score, a week after setting it
6|4.body: Medical Tent Mafia scored 80.36, under the 84.18 it posted in week 5, with Efton Chism starting for 0.00, Olamide Zaccheaus for 0.84, Josh Cameron for 1.84 and Cam Ward at 6.78. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 23.65 was 29% of the total, and the best possible lineup was 91.34. Erin Jacobs ended a five-game losing streak at 134.64, 41.54 above an honest projection, on Tre Tucker's 27.45, Matthew Golden's 21.65 and Michael Mayer's 19.50, a week after Mayer made 1.20; Najee Harris started for 0.20 with DeMario Douglas' 18.35 on the bench again. Erin won by 54.28, Mitch is 0-11, and Erin leads the all-time series 3-1.

6|5.headline: Michael Penix scores 23.10 for Jake Bogardus, and Matt Bova wins the closest game of the week
6|5.body: Jake Bogardus got 23.10 from Michael Penix at superflex and lost to Love's Shack anyway, 141.60 to 129.53, in the closest game of the week. Patrick Mahomes made 10.48, Bucky Irving 5.90 against a 14.84 projection and Terry McLaurin 3.70, and Bogardus finished at his season low, 2.75 under the median. Matt Bova beat an honest projection by 35.43 with Jordan Love at 20.24, Carnell Tate at 18.00 and Hunter Henry at 16.55, and left 5.61 on the table, the least of the week. Matt is 4-7, and the all-time series is level at 2-2.

6|6.headline: Jared Hayes benches Tyler Shough the week he scores 26.96, and wins by 48 anyway
6|6.body: A week after his -0.16, Tyler Shough went for 26.96 on the SirWinsAlot bench, next to Colston Loveland's 20.75, while Juwan Johnson started at tight end for 0.00; Hayes left 36.86 on the table. Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 and Jonathan Taylor's 21.10 got him to 140.49 anyway. Duane Gillenwater followed his season high with his season low, 91.93: Derrick Henry made 4.50 against an 18.12 projection, Jake Ferguson 3.80, Tyjae Spears 1.55, and Drake Maye's 25.80 was 28% of the total. Hayes won by 48.56, is 9-2, and has his first win over Duane in five meetings; Duane leads the all-time series 4-1.

7|1.headline: Mitch Blackwell falls to 0-14 as Sam LaPorta makes 3.30 with Eli Raridon's 16.10 on the bench
7|1.body: SirWinsAlot scored 156.99, within a point of an honest projection, on Colston Loveland's 22.15, Caleb Williams' 22.12 and Javonte Williams' 21.50, while Juwan Johnson started at tight end for 1.95. Medical Tent Mafia scored 84.64, 28.02 below an honest projection: Cam Ward made 5.74, LaPorta made 3.30 against a 16.18 projection with Raridon on the bench, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 30.30 was 36% of the total. Hayes won by 72.35, the biggest margin of the week, moves to 12-2, and leads the all-time series 3-2; Mitch is 0-14.

7|2.headline: Jake Blackwell starts Brock Purdy's 12.02 over Joe Burrow's 28.88, and Jake Bogardus takes the upset
7|2.body: BoKnows723 scored 163.97, 9.03 above an honest projection, with five running backs combining for 87.45, led by Bucky Irving's 23.50, and Michael Penix's 20.42 covering for Patrick Mahomes' 6.00; Mason Taylor's 27.45 sat on the bench behind Greg Dulcich. Nacua Matata posted its season low, 126.54, 37.51 below an honest projection and the worst miss of the week: Purdy started at superflex over Burrow, DeVonta Smith started for 0.00, and Kenneth Walker made 8.45 against a 19.74 projection. Jake Blackwell left 46.08 on the table, the most of the week, and his best lineup, 172.62, would have won by 8.65. Bogardus won by 37.43, is 9-5, and leads the all-time series 3-1.

7|3.headline: Erin Jacobs starts Justin Herbert on a bye, and Duane Gillenwater wins the lowest-scoring game of the season
7|3.body: Trade Block Maye! scored 121.49, under the median and 24.69 below an honest projection, but Drake Maye's 29.44 and Quinshon Judkins' 23.15 were plenty; Derrick Henry made 5.40, Aaron Jones 3.10, and Rashid Shaheed started for 1.88 with Caleb Douglas' 21.75 on the bench. Erin's 86.73 was her season low: Herbert started at quarterback for 0.00 with the Chargers off, Michael Mayer played superflex, and Tre Tucker's 21.80 did most of the lifting. The two combined for 208.22, the fewest points in any game this season. Duane won by 34.76, is 3-11, and leads the all-time series 6-0.

7|4.headline: Trey McBride and Bo Nix score 59.63 between them, and Chris Bova is 13-1
7|4.body: Titsburg Feelers scored 169.78, 14.56 below an honest projection, and won anyway: McBride made 30.35, Nix 29.28 and CeeDee Lamb 23.90, which covered Garrett Wilson's 4.35 and Jahmyr Gibbs' 15.30 against a 27.12 projection. Chris Merkel got 27.95 from Zay Flowers and 22.50 from Omar Cooper, then gave it back at tight end, where Isaiah Likely and Mark Andrews made 9.50 combined, and at superflex, where Baker Mayfield made 6.66. His 135.89 finished just under the 141.90 median. Chris Bova won by 33.89, is 7-0 head to head and 13-1 overall, and leads the all-time series 3-2.

7|5.headline: Matt Bova beats the median and half the league, but not Tony Pollard's 35.75
7|5.body: TurtleNeckTie scored 181.71, the week's high and Andrew's best of the season, 30.54 above an honest projection and the best mark of the week: Pollard made 35.75 against a 15.05 projection, Jameson Williams 26.10 and Dak Prescott 23.28, which made Nico Collins' 1.60 a footnote. Love's Shack scored 147.92, 18.31 above an honest projection, behind Tee Higgins' 28.80 and two tight ends at 32.40 combined, and lost by 33.79. Matt still took the median win and is 6-8. Andrew is 10-4 and leads the all-time series 4-1.

7|6.headline: Bryce Young makes 7.42 with Malik Willis' 28.02 on the bench, and Nick Bova takes the upset by 40
7|6.body: Nabers in Paris scored 160.87, 8.16 above an honest projection, on KC Concepcion's 22.45, Christian McCaffrey's 21.00 and Kirk Cousins' 20.40; Jalen Coker started for 1.65 against a 15.92 projection. Nick Merkel finished 33.74 below an honest projection at 120.30: Young started at superflex over Willis, Jalen Royals made 0.00, Tyler Higbee 3.40, and Bijan Robinson 15.70 against a 24.20 projection, which buried Luther Burden's 24.70 and Geno Smith's 23.48. Nick Bova won by 40.57, is 7-7, and leads the all-time series 3-1; Nick Merkel is 3-11.
